description: the Australian Government should call for an immediate and permanent ceasefire to end the humanitarian disaster in Gaza that began in October 2023, which is now the subject of an ongoing case in the International Court of Justice (ICJ), in which South Africa is accusing Israel of genocide

name: introducing a Pacific Engagement Visa (PEV)
description: the federal government should introduce a permanent Pacific Engagement Visa (PEV) to encourage more permanent migration to Australia from Pacific Island countries

name: revoking citizenship of dual nationals involved with terrorism offences by the courts
description: the federal government should give the Minister for Home Affairs the power to apply to the courts to revoke the citizenship of people who have dual nationality (that is, are also citizens of another country) if they take part in certain terrorism-related offences [NOTE: this policy is related to an older policy titled "Revoking citizenship of dual nationals involved with terrorism offences by the minister"]

name: considering motions on Gaza (2023-26) (procedural)
description: the federal government should suspend the usual procedural rules - known as standing orders - that would otherwise prevent our representatives from considering and voting on motions related to the humanitarian disaster in Gaza that began in October 2023 and which is now the subject of an ongoing case in the International Court of Justice (ICJ), in which South Africa is accusing Israel of genocide

name: up to 12 months of paid parental leave by 2030
description: the federal government should amend the law to extend paid parental leave to up to 12 months by 2030

name: carbon capture, storage and sequestration
description: the federal government should encourage the development of carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies

name: the federal government calling for a release of Israeli hostages in Gaza (2023-25)
description: the Australian Government should call for the immediate release of Israeli hostages abducted in October 2023 and currently held in Gaza by Hamas and other groups

name: recognising the State of Palestine
description: the federal government should officially recognise the State of Palestine

name: Build to Rent (BTR)
description: the federal government should address the rental crisis by supporting Build to Rent (BTR) with tax incentives, so as to encourage the development of more multi-apartment buildings where the apartments are rented out (usually through a single management entity) rather than sold

name: banning the sale of non-therapeutic vapes
description: the federal government should restrict the importation, domestic manufacture, supply, commercial possession and advertisement of non-therapeutic and disposable vaping goods

name: treating COVID vaccine status as a protected attribute
description: the federal government should introduce anti-discrimination laws so that a person cannot be discriminated against on the basis of their COVID vaccine status

name: vehicle efficiency standards
description: the federal government should introduce a vehicle efficiency standard (also known as a fuel efficiency or a vehicle carbon emissions standard)

name: banning politicial deepfakes
description: the federal government should introduce laws to ban the use of deepfakes in political advertising in the lead up to elections

name: placing the CFMEU into administration
description: the federal government should put the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union (CFMEU) into administration

name: capping international student numbers at universities
description: the minister should have the power to place a cap on the number of international students admitted to Australian universities

name: For increased domestic gas supply
description: The Federal Government should support increased investment in domestic gas supply to enable cheaper gas for households, manufactuers and to support renewables for power generation.

name: making price gouging illegal
description: the federal government should introduce laws to prohibit corporations from engaging in conduct that is likely to result in excessive prices for goods and services for consumers

name: introducing digital ID
description: the federal government should introduce legislation to establish digital ID in Australia

name: reducing tax concessions for high socio-economic status
description: the federal government should reduce tax concessions for high earners and those of high socio-economic status

name: full implementation of the Genocide Convention
description: the federal government should fully implement the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide into Australian domestic law

name: targetting homelessness in specific vulnerable groups
description: the federal government should work to address homelessness in specific vulnerable groups, such as older women and First Nations people

name: criminalising wage theft
description: Employers should be able to be criminally prosecuted for intentionally stealing the wages of their employees.

name: Building Fusion Energy Power plants instead of Nuclear Fission power plants in Australia and ASEAN
description:
The Federal government must invest privately and publically in research and develop into Fusion Energy's peaceful power generation. 

The federal government is risking Australia becoming a backwater community in the ASEAN region.

In an Australian context, Nuclear only refers to Thorium and Fission, not FUSION ENERGY.
The government is failing the Australian taxpayer and hampering Australian growth.
Australia can build a Fusion power plant now.

name: Developing Fusion for Australia in Australia for Australias future.
description:
Growing Australia's Industry, Supporting Immigration, and Developing Fusion Energy
Contents
1.	Introduction:	1
2.	Industry Growth Strategy	1
3.	Immigration as a Growth Enabler:	1
4.	Fusion Energy Development and Challenges:	1
5.	Barriers to Fusion Energy Development	1
6.	Addressing Concerns about Australia's Industry and Immigration Appeal:	1
7.	Defence Capability Enhancement:	1
8.	Global and Political Considerations:	1
9.	Why Fusion Energy is Superior to Fission	1
10.	Economic & Environmental Benefits:	1
11.	Conclusion:	1

1.	Introduction: 

Australia has the potential to become a global leader in advanced industries, sustainable energy, and skilled workforce development. By strategically integrating industry growth, immigration policies, and cutting-edge energy research, Australia can enhance economic growth, global competitiveness, and energy security.
2.	Industry Growth Strategy: 

Advanced Manufacturing: Invest in high-tech sectors like semiconductors, robotics, and space technology. • Green Technology & Renewable Energy: Expand battery storage, solar panel production, and hydrogen-based industries. • Mining & Resources Innovation: Promote sustainable mining and value-added processing. • Infrastructure Development: Strengthen transport and digital infrastructure.
3.	Immigration as a Growth Enabler: 

Skilled Migration Pathways: Attract top talent in STEM, engineering, and energy research. • Regional Immigration Initiatives: Encourage skilled immigrants to support regional economies. • Entrepreneurial & Start-up Support: Introduce visas for entrepreneurs and investors. • Education & Workforce Integration: Enhance pathways for international students to join the workforce.
4.	Fusion Energy Development and Challenges:

R&D Investments: Establish national fusion research centres in collaboration with global partners. • Public-Private Partnerships: Support private-sector investment in fusion start-ups. • International Collaboration: Partner with ITER, MIT, HB11, and other leading research organisations. • Regulatory Framework & Safety Standards: Develop clear policies for responsible fusion energy deployment.
5.	Barriers to Fusion Energy Development: 

Underfunding: Lack of public funding has hindered progress. • Policy Inconsistencies: No cohesive national strategy exists. • Regulatory Barriers: Unclear regulations deter investment. • Lack of Research Infrastructure: No large-scale fusion research facilities in Australia. • Limited Industry Collaboration: Insufficient government incentives for private-sector partnerships. • Low Public Awareness & Political Will: Minimal advocacy for fusion energy development.
6.	Addressing Concerns about Australia's Industry and Immigration Appeal: 

Who Will Buy Australian-Manufactured Products? o Trade Partnerships: Strong agreements with China, the U.S., Japan, and the EU. o Competitive Advantage: High-quality, ethically sourced goods. o Emerging Industries: Growth in green technology, defence, and medical innovations. • Who Would Immigrate to Australia? o Quality of Life: High rankings in healthcare, education, and safety. o Economic Opportunities: Strong demand for skilled workers. o Political & Social Stability: A safe, democratic environment. o Research & Innovation Hubs: World-class opportunities in clean energy and manufacturing.
7.	Defence Capability Enhancement: 

Invest in modern defence technologies, cybersecurity, and intelligence capabilities to safeguard national interests. • Trade Defence: Establish policies to counter unfair tariffs and trade restrictions imposed by foreign governments, ensuring Australian industries remain competitive. • Energy Security: Reduce reliance on foreign energy imports by investing in domestic renewable and fusion energy resources. • Border Protection & Maritime Security: Strengthen border control mechanisms to safeguard Australia's sovereignty and economic interests. • Allied Partnerships: Expand strategic defence alliances with like-minded nations to enhance regional security. • Fusion Energy for Defence and Logistics: Develop fusion-based propulsion for submarines, surface maritime vessels, and rail transport to enhance defence logistics and trade efficiency. • Space Propulsion: Invest in fusion-powered space propulsion systems to establish leadership in space exploration and satellite deployment.
8.	Global and Political Considerations: 

Ukraine War Impact: Supply chain disruptions highlight domestic energy security needs. • U.S. Trade Policies: Protectionism requires Australia to diversify trade markets. • Ethnic Clashes in Australia: Strengthen integration policies to maintain social cohesion. • Upcoming Australian Federal Election: Policy decisions on industry, immigration, and energy will shape the nation's future.
9.	Why Fusion Energy is Superior to Fission: 

Safety: No long-lived radioactive waste or meltdown risks. • Fuel Abundance: Uses widely available deuterium and tritium. • Minimal Environmental Impact: No greenhouse gas emissions. • Higher Energy Yield: More efficient and sustainable. • Reduced Proliferation Risks: No weaponisable byproducts.
10.	Economic & Environmental Benefits: 

Household Budget Savings: Fusion Energy will significantly lower electricity costs due to its high efficiency and abundant fuel supply, reducing financial pressure on households. • Lower Construction Costs: An affordable and consistent energy supply will reduce the cost of building materials and manufacturing, making home construction more accessible. • Reduced Industrial and Farming Costs: Reliable, low-cost fusion energy will lower production expenses for industries and agriculture, increasing competitiveness and reducing consumer prices. • Job Creation: Expands employment across multiple sectors. • Energy Independence: Reduces reliance on fossil fuels. • Environmental Sustainability: Supports carbon neutrality goals. • Global Leadership: Positions Australia at the forefront of clean energy innovation.
11.	Conclusion: 
By integrating industrial growth, strategic immigration policies, and fusion energy development, Australia can secure a prosperous and globally competitive future. Overcoming barriers to fusion energy, strengthening trade relationships, and attracting skilled immigrants will ensure economic resilience, energy security, and technological leadership. Navigating geopolitical challenges and trade shifts will be key to sustaining long-term national progress.
